limitations: Both heads use the same subject, object and nonentity-context means. Empty context contributes a zero vector before centering. The 4,192 fit rows determine the centering, block scales and 25-pair vocabulary. The typed head adds a one-hot vector that is all zeros for an unseen pair.

The analytic gradient matches the stated 40-class mean cross-entropy objective with L2 regularization on weights and bias. Both fits retain all 40 output columns and use only pooled features and, for the typed arm, type-pair indicators as predictors. The script requires optimizer success and a gradient infinity norm at most 1e-6 for both heads before sealing their coefficients and scoring either evaluation set.

The script scores all 4,000 assessment rows and all 19,584 development VALID rows. It checks the reconstructed hard type rule against the frozen macro-F1 and correct count. Each arm requires both a strict gain in macro-F1 over classes 1 through 39 and more paired repairs than damages. The separate typed-versus-untyped comparison measures macro-F1 gain only.

Prior exposure of both TRAIN subsets, reuse of development VALID and the historical full-TRAIN fit budget limit a positive result to an exploratory comparison. A negative result applies only to these fixed fits. This static review relies on the accepted retrospective row lineage. Staged hashes, numerical convergence and comparator agreement remain execution-time checks.
